summary: Mission Helium-3 is a 3D educational space mission game, playable in the browser, made by a team of Kodland programming students. Humanity's electricity demand keeps growing and we need clean energy sources without radioactive waste; fusion with helium-3 is a promising option, but helium-3 is almost absent on Earth while the solar wind has deposited it in lunar regolith. The player runs a complete mission from concept to operation: launches from an Earth base, handles a chemical engine failure by talking with Mission Control and reading spacecraft telemetry, lands on the Moon with a helium-3 plasma engine, mines regolith with a rover, and operates the real seven-stage helium-3 production process inside a lunar station (beneficiation, heating to 700-1000 C, gas capture, cryogenic isotope separation and storage). Each stage requires engineering decisions, and the player must manage limited resources: suit oxygen, regolith (some rocks contain no helium-3) and the 15-20 fuel capsules needed to lift off with the engine at its limit and return to Earth. It turns abstract mission trade-offs into hands-on play.
details:
WHAT IT DOES: Mission Helium-3 lets students experience a whole space mission, from concept to operation, as one continuous first-person game with third-person cinematics. 1) Concept: the player starts in a launch-base control room where a screen explains the problem (growing electricity demand, pollution and radioactive waste from current sources) and the mission plan. 2) Launch: the player walks to the pad, climbs the 15 m service tower, boards the rocket and watches a countdown as the tower arms release the vehicle. 3) Cruise and failure: the chemical engine fails leaving the atmosphere; in zero-g the player talks with Mission Control by choosing answers that must match the spacecraft monitor (fuel, engines, damage, navigation). 4) Lunar operations: the ship lands on a lunar pad using a helium-3 plasma engine; the astronaut walks in 1.62 m/s2 gravity, drives a mining rover among 50 rocks (some basalt rocks contain no helium-3), and delivers regolith to a reactor hopper. 5) Production: inside a lunar station, each room hosts one stage of the real helium-3 process, and it only works if the player chooses correct engineering values: sieve mesh under 150 micrometers with magnetic and electrostatic separators; furnace between 700 and 1000 C; filter, compress and cool the gases in order; repeated cryogenic distillation at -271 C to raise purity from 0.04% to 99.9%; and filling capsules between 150 and 300 bar. 6) Return: the ship needs 15-20 capsules (random each game); the plasma engine works at its limit to reach the 2.38 km/s lunar escape velocity and lands back at the Earth base, where the result screen explains that leftover helium-3 will be used for energy research.

RESOURCE MANAGEMENT AND TRADE-OFFS: suit oxygen (7 minutes outside, refilled in the station airlock), rover cargo capacity, rocks without helium-3, capsule count and engine limits.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT: it turns abstract mission trade-offs (propulsion, resources, communications, gravity) and the science of lunar helium-3 into hands-on learning for children and teens, in Spanish, playable in any computer browser with no installation.

TOOLS: Godot 4.7 (GDScript, web export), Terrain3D for the lunar terrain, Blender and downloaded 3D models, Mixamo for astronaut animations, GitHub for teamwork and GitHub Pages, itch.io for publishing.

CREATIVITY: real industrial steps of helium-3 extraction become playable consoles; a radio dialogue with Mission Control uses Quindar tones; floating objects in zero-g; low-gravity walking; a fully playable mission loop from Earth to the Moon and back.

TEAM: Kimberly Selena Sandoval Guato, Jentsel Arnold Aguilar Aguilera, Darwin Emil Alvarez Miranda, José Miguel Tang Ly, Mariano Carazo and Camilo Muñoz Bermudez (team lead), students of Kodland programming school. Play: https://kodlandcamubermu.itch.io/mision-helio-3 - Code: https://github.com/Camubermu/mision-helio-3

SI USE: an AI assistant helped write and debug part of the code and the in-game texts.
